lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: — nothing. A warm, total nothing, like the inside of a held breath. You could stay here. You have, perhaps, stayed here a long time already.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Cold. Wet stone under the cheek. Salt. Get up. GET UP.

responses.text: [Stay in the nothing a little longer.]

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Yes. Don't rush it. Whatever is out there waited all night; it can wait one more minute. Catalogue what you know before you let the light in.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: What you know is a short list. You are horizontal. You are outdoors. You are, regrettably, alive.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: And you are not alone. There's someone very close. They are not breathing the way you are. They are not breathing at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Grey light, the colour of dishwater. Rain you can't feel yet, only hear — a million soft collisions on the harbour. You are on a quay of black, weeping stone, and a man is lying ten feet away with his face turned to the planks.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: His coat is good wool, gone to ruin in the wet. One shoe off. No blood. The water around him is the wrong shape — it ran toward him, not away.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Reasonable questions. Here is the inventory of answers: none. There is a hole where your name should be. Reach into it and it bites.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: But the hands. The hands remember something. There's a weight they're used to — a small brass weight, a thumb-flick. You've done a hundred small violent things and the body kept every one.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: Enough. Stand up. There is a dead man and an audience, and a man on his back in the rain commands no one.

passiveChecks.label: Intuition — feel for the shape of who you were

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: V. K. Two letters, like two knocks on a door you're afraid to answer. They mean something. They mean YOU.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You get your feet under you. The quay tilts, steadies. Up the plankway a woman in a bailswoman's oilskin watches you with the patience of someone deciding whether you are a problem or a tool.

lines.speaker: the_body
lines.text: So. The Watch sends a man who sleeps next to the body. That's either very good or very bad police work, and I genuinely can't tell which.

lines.speaker: attribute
lines.text: She called you the Watch. There is a badge in your coat. You don't remember earning it. Decide, quickly, whether you're going to be the man she thinks you are.
